items.text: The German national football team has had a long-standing partnership with Adidas. They wore Adidas gear even during past World Cups. However, the recent announcement that Nike will replace Adidas as the official partner from 2027 onwards came as a surprise. Sports expert Mark Meadows explained the reasons behind this unexpected change. Financial struggles, worsened by recent team performance and the pandemic, played a significant role. Despite Adidas’s historical importance, the allure of Nike’s offer was too strong for the German team. Both fans and Adidas are bewildered by such a sudden decision. The German Football Association defended its choice; however, this shift highlights the key role of money in sports. Yet, there’s a possibility of reverting to Adidas in the future, because Nike’s contract ends in 2034. Difficult words: allure (attraction), bewildered (very puzzled, confused), revert (to return to a previous state, practice, etc.). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The German football team had a close link with Adidas for years, even during successful World Cup campaigns. But recently, the German Football Association announced that Nike will replace Adidas as the official partner from 2027 onwards. It was a big surprise for both German fans and Adidas. A sports expert explained that financial problems and recent team performance could be the main reasons for the change. The German Football Association said that there were mainly financial reasons. Adidas was always very important, but Nike’s offer was more attractive. This shows the impact of money on sports. There is a chance of returning to Adidas, as Nike’s contract lasts until 2034. Difficult words: replace (to take the place of something), performance (how well a person, team, machine, and so on does a piece of work or activity), contract (a deal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For many years, the German football team only wears Adidas. Even during World Cups. But the news comes. It surprises everybody, fans, and Adidas too. Nike will replace Adidas in 2027. An expert explains why. The team has problems with money. Also, it does not play very well now. A change must come. The German Football Association speaks about money. This shows how money affects sports. Still, there is a chance of going back to Adidas in the future. The deal with Nike will end in 2034. Difficult words: replace (to take the place of something), affect (to have an impact on something or someone). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Carlo Del Buono and Jose Cianni have turned farming crickets into a successful business venture in Italy. Nutrinsect, their startup, produces cricket flour, which is high in protein and environmentally friendly. Initially importing crickets, Cianni’s farm now sustains itself, producing two tons of cricket flour monthly. Despite initial skepticism , Nutrinsect’s products quickly sold out after Italy approved their use in food. Del Buono, a pizza maker, experiments with cricket pizza, adding a small portion of cricket powder to the dough. Although some are hesitant about trying cricket-based products, Del Buono remains optimistic and plans to introduce cricket pizza to his menu soon. Difficult words: business venture (a business or project that involves risk, usually for profit), sustain (to cause to continue without interruption), skepticism (a doubtful attitude or disbelief). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Italy, Carlo Del Buono and Jose Cianni run a successful business farming crickets . Their startup, Nutrinsect, produces cricket flour, which is high in protein and environmentally friendly . At first, they imported crickets, but now, Cianni’s farm produces two tons of cricket flour monthly. After Italy approved their use in food, Nutrinsect’s products quickly sold out. Del Buono, a pizza maker, experiments with cricket pizza, and he adds a small amount of cricket powder to the dough . Despite some doubts, Del Buono plans to add cricket pizza to his menu soon. Difficult words: cricket (a leaping insect which makes a sound with his legs), flour (a powder we use to make bread, cakes, and pasta), dough (a thick mixture of flour and water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Italy, Carlo Del Buono and Jose Cianni run a successful business. They have a cricket farm. Their startup, Nutrinsect, produces cricket flour . Cricket flour has a lot of protein. It does not hurt the natural world. At first, they import crickets. But Cianni’s farm now produces two tons of cricket flour every month. In Italy, it is okay to use crickets in food. People buy Nutrinsect’s products a lot. Del Buono is a pizza maker. They try to make cricket pizza. They put cricket powder into the dough . Some people do not like this idea. But Del Buono plans to have cricket pizza on his menu soon. Difficult words: cricket (an insect which makes a sound with his legs), flour (a powder which we use to make bread, cakes, or pasta), dough (a thick substance from flour and water). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Following a catastrophic fire in 2019, Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris embarked on a meticulous five-year restoration journey. Despite facing challenges such as pandemic delays and changes in leadership, significant progress has been achieved. The recent removal of scaffolding revealed a new spire adorned with a golden rooster and a cross, marking a symbolic step forward in the cathedral’s resurrection . Restoration efforts have been comprehensive, including rebuilding the organ, selecting oak trees for the spire, and restoring stained glass windows. The works demonstrate the dedication to reviving this historic landmark. Despite setbacks, the project is on track for completion by the end of 2024, signifying a remarkable milestone in the cathedral’s history. Difficult words: meticulous (very careful and precise), adorned (made more beautiful), resurrection (bringing something back into use or existence). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

After a devastating fire in 2019, workers began to restore Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris. The work started five years ago and there were many problems like pandemic delays. But the works are continuing and it seems that they could finish by the end of 2024. When workers removed the scaffolding , they found a new spire with a golden rooster and a cross. Workers rebuilt the organ and restored stained glass windows. Although there are many problems, once workers finish, it will mark an important moment in the cathedral’s history. Difficult words: devastating (causing great damage), scaffolding (a structure on the outside of the building which workers use while building), spire (a tall narrow structure which rises to a point, usually on a church). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2019, a big fire damages Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris, France. Since then, people work hard to fix it. There are many problems, for example, delays and changes in leading the project. But now, the work is almost at its end. There is a new spire with a golden rooster and a cross. Workers also fix an organ. They change the windows. Many people believe that Notre Dame will open again by the end of 2024. It will be an important moment for the cathedral and French people. Difficult words: delay (when something happens later than it should), spire (a tall narrow structure, usually in a church), rooster (a male chicken). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite efforts to curb it, the fentanyl crisis in the US persists, claiming over 100,000 lives annually, mainly due to synthetic opioids like fentanyl, which can be 50 times more potent than heroin. Brian, a former addict, shared his harrowing experience of addiction while living on the streets of San Francisco for three years. His life revolved around acquiring drugs to avoid withdrawal symptoms, often resorting to theft to fund his habit. Witnessing deaths from overdoses became commonplace. Brian’s health deteriorated , suffering from infections and septic legs, but he managed to survive and has been clean for nearly a year. His story sheds light on the grim reality of addiction amidst a rising death toll from synthetic opioids. Difficult words: resort (to turn to something to resolve a difficult situation), deteriorate (to become progressively worse), septic (infected). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The fentanyl crisis in the US is serious. There were over 100,000 deaths reported last year, mostly due to opioids like fentanyl. They are much stronger than heroin. Brian comes from San Francisco and he was addicted to fentanyl. He was homeless for three years. He needed drugs so badly that he stole things to have money for them. He saw many people die from overdoses . Brian’s health got worse and his legs got infected. He was lucky to survive and stopped taking drugs almost one year ago. His story tells us about the troubles of addicted people and about how dangerous opioids can be. Difficult words: opioid (a type of drug which reduces pain), addicted (when a person is not able to stop taking drugs or doing something), overdose (taking too much of a drug). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the US, many people are dying from drugs . People take opioids. These are drugs which reduce pain. One of them is fentanyl. It is very strong. It is stronger than heroin. Brian lives in San Francisco. In the past, he takes fentanyl. He lives on the streets for three years. He needs money for drugs. He steals things. Sometimes, he sees people die from taking too many drugs. Brian gets sick. He almost dies. Brian is lucky to be alive. He stops taking drugs almost a year ago. His story tells us how dangerous drugs are. Last year, opioids kill 100,000 people in the US. Difficult words: drug (a substance which makes you feel different), reduce (to make something smaller), steal (to take something what is not yours). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nvidia, a leading chipmaker, showcased its newest AI chip, the B200, at its annual developer conference, signaling its intent to maintain its supremacy in the AI industry. The B200 chip, announced by CEO Jensen Huang in Silicon Valley, promises to be 30 times faster at certain tasks compared to its predecessors . Huang also introduced new software tools aimed at simplifying the sale of AI models for developers, potentially benefiting companies reliant on Nvidia’s technology. Despite the innovative announcements, Nvidia’s stock experienced a slight decline, suggesting the updates didn’t excite investors as expected. Moreover, Nvidia is transitioning from selling individual chips to offering comprehensive systems, which could redefine its market strategy amidst growing competition and the self-reliance trend among its largest clients. However, industry analysts forecast a minor dip in Nvidia’s market share in 2024 due to emerging rivals and the in-house chip production efforts of major tech firms. Difficult words: supremacy (the state of being the most powerful or superior), predecessor (a thing that has come before), dip (decrease). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Nvidia showed off a new AI chip, the B200, which is very fast and powerful. This happened at a big meeting for developers in California. The company’s boss, Jensen Huang, said that this chip is much better than the old ones and it can be 30 times faster. Nvidia also made new software to help people sell AI better. Even though these are big news, Nvidia’s shares went down a little bit after the announcement . The company is also starting to sell complete systems instead of just chips. This change comes because other companies start to make their chips, which could challenge Nvidia. Still, Nvidia is trying to stay ahead in the technology market by making its products better and working with big companies. Difficult words: share (one of the parts of a company), announcement (a public or formal statement about something important), challenge (to test someone’s skills or abilities). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Nvidia is a big company. They make chips . They make a new chip called B200. It is very fast. Nvidia’s boss says that it can be 30 times faster than other chips. The boss talks about it in California. The company also makes a new software. This helps people use AI better. But Nvidia thinks that people will be more excited about the news. It does not happen. Nvidia is also making big systems, not just chips. Some companies want to make their chips. This can be hard for Nvidia. But Nvidia is still trying to be the best. They want to work with other big companies. Difficult words: chip (a small piece of technology which has a lot of computer power), excited (very happy about something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

James Crumbley, father of Ethan Crumbley, the teen responsible for the Oxford high school shooting in Michigan, the United States, has been found guilty of involuntary manslaughter. This groundbreaking verdict holds a parent criminally responsible for their child’s actions, setting a precedent in the country. During the trial, prosecutors emphasized that James failed to secure the gun used in the shooting, despite having a legal duty to protect others from potential harm. While Michigan lacked a storage law at the time, James was deemed accountable for his negligence . Although Ethan exhibited concerning behavior, including disturbing drawings and cries for help, the Crumbleys didn’t take appropriate action. The verdict, delivered after a full day of deliberations, sends a powerful message about accountability in cases of gun violence. Despite this legal outcome, the tragic loss of four students serves as a poignant reminder of the devastating consequences of such incidents. Difficult words: deemed (considered or judged), negligence (failure to take proper care over something), poignant (causing or having a very sharp feeling of sadness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

James Crumbley, father of Ethan Crumbley, who killed four people in the Oxford high school shooting in Michigan, is guilty of involuntary manslaughter . This is the first case in the US when a court says that parents are responsible for their child’s actions. James did not secure the gun which his son used in the shooting, but it was his duty. Michigan did not have a law about this at the time of the shooting, but the court said that James was careless. Ethan’s mental state was bad but his parents did not help him in any way. The verdict is very important for future cases. It is important to make parents responsible for their children’s actions. Difficult words: involuntary (when you do something without planning it or choosing to do it), manslaughter (killing a person), verdict (what a court decides). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ethan Crumbley kills four people in the Oxford high school shooting. The school is in Michigan, the United States. The boy is 17 years old now. He will stay in prison all his life. Now a court says that Ethan’s father is guilty , too. This is the first time in the US that a parent is responsible for what their child does. The problem is that James does not keep his gun in a safe place. His son uses the gun to kill people. Before that, Ethan has mental problems. He calls for help. But his parents do nothing. A court says that parents must be responsible for their children. Difficult words: guilty (when a court says that you do something wrong), responsible (to have control over something or someone), mental (related to the mind or thinking). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The European Commission, led by President Ursula von der Leyen, is proposing revisions to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in response to widespread farmer protests across Europe. These revisions aim to reduce governmental control over EU farmers and provide them with greater flexibility to comply with environmental regulations. The protests, which have occurred in countries like Spain, France, the Netherlands, and Belgium, are primarily against EU regulations on climate change, imports from non-EU countries, and production costs. The Commission believes that the proposed changes strike a balance between supporting sustainable farming practices and addressing the concerns of farmers. Additionally, the revisions include measures to improve the position of EU farmers in the food supply chain. Von der Leyen emphasized the importance of these proposals in supporting farmers amidst various challenges and expressed confidence that they were developed in collaboration with stakeholders , Member States, and Members of the European Parliament. Difficult words: comply (to follow rules or standards), stakeholder (an individual or group with an interest or concern in the matter at hand). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The European Commission responded to protests by farmers across Europe. President Ursula von der Leyen is proposing changes to Europe’s policy. These changes should lessen governmental control over EU farmers and offer them more flexibility in meeting environmental regulations. The protests took place in countries such as Spain, France, the Netherlands, and Belgium, and they are mainly against EU regulations on climate change, imports from non-EU countries, and production costs. The Commission believes that the changes will bring a balance between sustainable farming and the problems of farmers. Von der Leyen said that the changes were necessary and that the Commission developed them with the help of farmers, individuals, and governments. Difficult words: lessen (to make or become less), flexibility (the ability to change something easily), sustainable farming (farming in such a way to protect the natural world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

European Commission wants to change farming in Europe. This happens because many farmers in Europe are unhappy. They protest. The protests happen in Spain, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, and other countries. Farmers do not like EU rules about climate change, imports , and costs. The changes would give farmers more freedom and less control from governments. The Commission says that the changes are fair to farmers. They help them work better. President Ursula von der Leyen says these ideas come from talking to farmers, leaders, and other important people. Difficult words: import (things which one country buys or brings in from another country), freedom (when someone is free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Biologists in New Zealand made a remarkable discovery, uncovering approximately 100 new species in a rift deep beneath the sea. Among these organisms are unidentified creatures and a peculiar species known as a ‘sea-pig’. Their expedition aimed to find species before they vanished forever. They encountered various new creatures, including a large sea cucumber and unique sea cucumbers with leg-like appendages . Using cameras, they observed known species at unexpected depths, such as the taningia danae, with its distinctive features. The team also discovered new species of octopus and coral, along with unidentified creatures. Previously overlooked, the Bounty Trough is now recognized as a rich area for scientific exploration. Difficult words: peculiar (unusual or strange), appendage (an additional part attached to something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Biologists in New Zealand found about 100 new species deep in the sea. There were many unidentified ones and a creature called a ‘sea-pig’. Scientists hoped to discover species before they disappear ed forever. They found many creatures, like large sea cucumbers and unique sea cucumbers with leg-like parts. With the help of cameras, they saw known species at big depths. They also found new types of octopus and coral and some unknown creatures. The area didn’t seem too interesting for scientists but now, they recognize it as rich and want to explore it more. Difficult words: unidentified (something what people didn’t know before), disappear (to not exist anymore), recognize (to accept something formally). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In New Zealand, scientists find many new animals deep in the sea. It happens in an area which they do not find interesting. But now, they see it as a good place to explore . Scientists find about 100 new animals. They do not know some of them at all. There is also a strange animal called a ‘sea-pig’. These are big sea cucumbers and sea cucumbers with legs. Scientists want to find these animals before they disappear forever. But they do not expect to find so many new species . They also saw known animals in unexpected places. The area is now seen as a good place for scientists to explore more. Difficult words: explore (to travel through a new area and learn about it), disappear (to not exist anymore), species (a type of living thing). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite efforts to deliver aid to Gaza through airdrops, the UN warns it’s insufficient to prevent famine for the 500,000 desperate people in need. Airdrops pose risks, with reports of fatalities due to falling packages. Jeremy Konyndyk, a disaster relief expert, highlights the high cost and logistical challenges of airdrops compared to other methods. Successful airdrops require compact, durable items and safe drop zones. Coordination on the ground is crucial for effective distribution. While airdrops have been useful in natural disasters and conflict zones, challenges in Gaza hinder their effectiveness. Despite accusations of aid obstruction, governments continue airdrops as a symbolic gesture of seriousness. Long-term solutions, like a ceasefire and political pressure to end the siege , are necessary to address the humanitarian crisis. Difficult words: coordination (the organization of different activities or people involved in something), hinder (to make it difficult for someone to do or for something to happen), siege (the surrounding of a place by an armed force to defeat those defending it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

There are problems with delivering aid to Gaza through airdrops. Airdrop means dropping food or other help from a plane. The UN warns that airdrops don’t stop famine for the 500,000 people in need. Also, when planes drop packages with help, they may hurt or even kill people on the ground. Airdrops are expensive and compared to other ways, they are not easy to do. For successful airdrops, there must be safe drop zones. Also, people on the ground need to organize the help, which is very difficult. Many people criticize this form of help, but governments continue airdrops to show support for Gaza. But airdrops will not solve the problem. Difficult words: aid (help), famine (when people have nothing to eat), continue (to keep doing something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Gaza need help. Some help comes from planes. Planes drop food and other things to people on the ground. This way of helping is called airdrops. But airdrops are difficult. It can happen that they hurt or even kill people. Also, someone must deal with the help on the ground. Such help is very expensive, too. But countries still do it. They want to show that they care. The UN says that airdrops will not stop hunger for 500,000 people. To solve the problem, we need peace and better ways to send help. Difficult words: drop (to let or make something fall), hunger (feeling or not having enough food), peace (when people or countries do not fight with each other). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scary footage captured the moment a plane lost a tire during takeoff on its way to Japan. The incident forced a United Airlines flight bound for Osaka to divert to Los Angeles International Airport. The falling tire damaged cars in the San Francisco airport parking lot. Fortunately, the Boeing 777-200 landed safely at LAX with no injuries reported among the 235 passengers and crew onboard. United Airlines arranged a new aircraft for the continuation of the journey. This incident adds to a series of mid-air problems involving Boeing planes operated by United Airlines, raising concerns about aviation safety. Difficult words: mid-air (above the ground), aviation (the flying or operating of aircraft). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A shocking incident happened when a plane bound for Japan lost a tire during takeoff. United Airlines diverted the flight to Los Angeles International Airport. The falling tire damaged cars in the San Francisco airport parking lot. Thankfully, the Boeing 777-200 landed safely at LAX, and there were no injuries among the passengers and crew. United Airlines arranged another plane for the passengers. There were several mid-air issues involving Boeing planes recently. This raised concerns about aviation safety. Difficult words: bound (going or ready towards a specified place), mid-air (above the ground), aviation (the flying or operating planes). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An incident happens on March 4. A plane is going to Osaka, Japan. But it loses a tire during takeoff . The plane must land in Los Angeles. United Airlines prepare another plane for the passengers . Luckily, no one gets hurt. The tire falls on cars in the airport parking lot. It damages some cars. This incident is one of several problems with Boeing planes recently. All of these incidents concern United Airlines. Some people worry that it is not safe to travel with United Airlines. Difficult words: takeoff (the moment when a plane leaves the ground), passenger (a person who travels on a bus, train, plane, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Young Russians reflect on Putin’s 24 years in power. Zaurbek, 27, views President Vladimir Putin as the key to Russia’s stability, while Egor, 18, criticizes the country’s leadership. Despite their differing opinions, both have never experienced a time when Putin wasn’t in power. Dubbed ‘Generation Putin’, young Russians like them reflect on Putin’s 24-year reign. Putin maintains high approval ratings , though youth are more critical of the country’s direction. Despite political tensions, many still support Putin, valuing stability and progress. Others, like Egor, challenge authority, advocating for change despite risks. These perspectives reveal the complexities of Russia’s political landscape under Putin’s long-standing rule. Difficult words: rating (a valuation or rank on a scale), complexity (the state of being intricate or complicated). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Young Russians, or so-called Generation Putin, say what they think about their president Vladimir Putin and his 24 years in power. Zaurbek, 27, believes that thanks to Putin, Russia is a stable country. Egor, 18, sees Russia’s leaders as unworthy . Both young men grew up under Putin’s rule and they have contrasting ideas on him. They also have different opinions about Russia’s future. Putin is still very popular, even among young people, but some of them start to worry about the future of their country. Their perspectives show how complicated Russia’s politics is. Difficult words: unworthy (something what people should not respect or like), contrasting (very different), perspective (a way of considering something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The so-called Generation Putin are young people. They live in Russia. Putin is their president all their lives. They do not know any other Russian president. Zaurbek is 27 years old. He thinks that Putin keeps Russia safe. Egor is 18 years old. He does not like Russia’s leaders . Both men always know Putin as the leader. Putin is in power for 24 years. Some young people like Putin. But others want change. They have different views , but they all grow up with Putin as the leader. Difficult words: leader (the person who leads others and tells them what to do), in power (when someone is the leader), view (the way how you see things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Akira Toriyama, the renowned creator of Dragon Ball, passed away at 68. Toriyama left behind a significant legacy, influencing manga worldwide, particularly the shonen genre. Dragon Ball serialized 40 years ago, became a global phenomenon, inspiring cartoons, films, and video games. Toriyama’s impact extended beyond entertainment, shaping art, and even political movements. His work contributed to the international popularity of manga, spreading Japanese culture globally. Notably, Dragon Ball’s characters and themes resonated with audiences worldwide, reflecting resilience and determination. Toriyama’s influence remains evident in the widespread adoption of manga aesthetics and tropes . His legacy endures as a pioneer of Japanese pop culture. Difficult words: serialized (published or broadcasted regularly), aesthetics (concerning beauty or the appreciation of beauty), trope (a significant theme). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The creator of Dragon Ball, Akira Toriyama, passed away at the age of 68. Dragon Ball was on TV 40 years ago and it became a big hit worldwide. There were cartoons as well as films. Toriyama’s work influenced the manga genre and inspired creations like Naruto and One Piece. Dragon Ball’s popularity increased internationally, and there were adaptations in many countries and languages. Toriyama introduced manga to people around the world. He had an impact not only on TV and cartoons but also on art and even politics. Through Dragon Ball, Toriyama spread Japanese culture globally, and his impact will continue. Difficult words: hit (a successful film book, song, and so on), inspire (to make someone feel they want to do something), adaptation (a film or play which someone does after reading a book). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Akira Toriyama is a Japanese artist. He creates Dragon Ball. He dies last week. He is 68 years old. Toriyama tells stories about a boy who collects magical balls to fight evil . Dragon Ball becomes famous worldwide. There are cartoons and films about the boy. Toriyama’s work has an impact on manga . Thanks to him, many Japanese people are interested in culture . His stories teach us not to give up. His work is important not only for other artists but also for changing politics. Toriyama’s characters are still popular today. Difficult words: evil (something very bad or harmful), manga (a style of Japanese comic books), culture (books, films, theatres, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

India’s passion for vintage cars was celebrated at the Oberoi Concours d’Elegance, showcasing pre-war European classics and iconic American Cadillacs. Owners, deeply devoted to their prized vehicles, competed for recognition in various categories at the luxurious Oberoi hotel. The event highlighted India’s significant role in the vintage car market, with a quarter of Rolls-Royce production in the 1930s being sold in India. Among the displayed cars, industrialist Godam Singa’s collection stood out, with rare and unique models like the Bentley 4 and Phantom 3. Indian royalty’s connections to these vintage cars added to their allure , with intricate details making each ride special. The event also honored Indian classics, including the iconic Maruti 800. Difficult words: vintage (old and of high quality), industrialist (a person involved in large-scale business), allure (the quality of being attractive or fascinating). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Indian people love vintage cars and they celebrated this love at the Oberoi Concours d’Elegance. People could see pre-war European classics and iconic American Cadillacs. Car owners competed at the luxurious Oberoi Hotel, which showed India’s big role in the vintage car market. In the 1930s, Rolls-Royce sold a quarter of its production in India. Godam Singa is a big businessman and he owns many vintage cars. His collection includes unusual models like the Bentley 4 and Phantom 3. At the event, people could also see Indian classics, such as the iconic Maruti 800. Difficult words: vintage (very old and of high quality), classic (a work of art or an object that people recognize and they know how good or important it is), collection (a group of things or people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in India love old cars. Car owners show their cars at the Oberoi Hotel. Some cars are from the time before the war. There are famous European cars and American Cadillacs. The cars are beautiful. One rich businessman called Godam Singa has many old cars. He has for example Bentley 4 or Phantom 3. These cars are not so famous. Many cars have special colors and details . There are Indian cars too. In the 1930s, a quarter of Rolls Royce cars go to India. Difficult words: rich (a person who has a lot of money), detail (a small part of decoration), quarter (25 percent). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

143 Indigenous women in Greenland are suing Denmark for implanting them with intrauterine devices in the 1960s and 1970s, seeking 5.8 million euros in compensation. They allege that Danish authorities violated their human rights, fitting them with contraceptive coils without consent. Each woman demands 40,000 euros. The devices aimed to control population growth, but many women were unaware or didn’t consent to the procedure. Despite an ongoing investigation initiated by Denmark and Greenland in 2022, the women pursue justice through the court, citing urgency due to their advancing age. This lawsuit adds to Denmark’s history of controversial actions in Greenland, including forced relocations and assimilation attempts. Difficult words: intrauterine (inside the uterus), contraceptive coil (a small T-shaped plastic and copper device that a doctor puts into a womb to stop a woman from getting pregnant), assimilation (integrating people, ideas, or culture into a wider society or culture). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

143 Indigenous women in Greenland are suing Denmark. They say that doctors implanted them with intrauterine devices without their permission in the 1960s and 1970s. The women ask for 5.8 million euros, 40,000 euros each. They claim that Danish authorities violated their rights because they wanted to control the growing population. An investigation started in 2022, but the women went to court. They want to solve the issue quickly because they are getting old. This problem is only one of Greenland’s actions against indigenous people, including forced relocation and attempts to integrate indigenous people into Danish society. Difficult words: intrauterine device (a small plastic and metal device that a doctor puts into a woman’s uterus so that she doesn’t get pregnant), violate (break a rule), relocation (moving to another place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

143 Indigenous women in Greenland are angry with Denmark. In the 1960s and 1970s, doctors in Denmark implant them devices. These small plastic and metal devices stop them from having babies. These women do not agree with it. It is possible that doctors do not tell them the truth. The women say that Denmark wants to control birth in the past. The women want money from Denmark. Every woman wants 40,000 euros. It makes 5.8 million euros altogether. This is not the only problem Denmark has with indigenous people in the past. They move indigenous people away. In some places, they force them to live among Danish people. Difficult words: indigenous (the first people who live in a place), implant (to put something in a person’s body), birth (when a baby is born). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

California’s affluent coastal communities face a threat as heavy rains trigger flash floods and coastal erosion, endangering multimillion-dollar homes perched on cliffs. Governor Gavin Newsom declared a state of emergency in eight counties, encompassing over 20 million people, as rainfall surpasses normal levels. Residents in cities like San Clemente and Dana Point nervously monitor their properties as landslides loom. However, Bitcoin’s recent rally, driven by institutional investment, contrasts sharply with the prolonged crypto winter of 2022. Flows into US spot bitcoin funds reached 2.2 billion dollars, with significant investment in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust. The rally was buoyed by expectations of a US interest rate cut and positive risk sentiment . Despite its volatility and limited real-world applications, companies like MicroStrategy and Reddit are adding crypto to their portfolios. Stablecoins issued by Tether have surpassed 100 billion dollars, offering stability amidst crypto price fluctuations. Difficult words: plummet (to fall rapidly), buoyed (supported), risk sentiment (how financial market participants are behaving and feeling), volatility (the quality of being likely to change suddenly and unpredictably). In Ecuador’s rainforest, researchers uncovered a groundbreaking discovery: a new species of the world’s largest snake, the green anaconda. Separated from its closest relatives for 10 million years, it maintains a striking resemblance . Dutch biologist Freek Vonk’s video showcases the enormity of these 6-meter reptiles, with specimens weighing up to 200 kilograms. Initially believed to be one species, the scientific journal Diversity recently unveiled a distinct species – the ‘northern green anaconda’. The finding sheds light on the genetic divergence between the two anaconda species, despite their identical appearance. This discovery helps understand the ecological impacts of oil spills in the region, as anacondas serve as indicators of environmental health and potential risks to human health. Difficult words: resemblance (similarity in appearance), enormity (very great size or importance), divergence (the situation in which two things become different). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The 30-year-old Juventus midfielder faced a provisional suspension last September following a drug test revealing elevated testosterone levels after a match. Italy’s national anti-doping tribunal issued the ban, effective until August 2027. Pogba, expectedly, plans to appeal against the ruling. This development could potentially signal the premature end of his illustrious career, with implications stretching beyond his footballing achievements. Despite flashes of brilliance, his career has been influenced by inconsistencies and injury setbacks. While Pogba maintains his innocence, the evidence against him presents a significant challenge to his appeal prospects. Difficult words: illustrious (well-known and respected for past achievements), stint (a period spent doing something), inconsistency (lack of uniformity or reliability). Hungary is about to implement what is considered the strictest immigration law in the European Union. The law, which replaces a longstanding one in effect for 16 years, places significant emphasis on prioritizing Hungarian citizens for employment opportunities, aiming to safeguard their job prospects. The law’s rationale lies in addressing the escalating influx of migrants to Hungary. The legislation orders that immigrants terminated from their jobs must leave the country within a strict six-day timeframe, facilitated by their employers. Moreover, family reunification for third-country nationals employed in Hungary is abolished . Residence permits are categorized based on skill levels, distinguishing between highly skilled and low-skilled workers. Additionally, the law introduces a novel concept termed the ‘golden visa’ offering residency to individuals making substantial investments in real estate within Hungary. Despite its intentions, the legislation faces opposition from left-wing political factions within Hungary’s parliament. Difficult words: rationale (the reasons or intentions that cause a particular set of beliefs or actions), facilitate (to make an action or process easier), abolish (to formally put an end to), novel (interestingly new or unusual). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A family reunion for immigrant workers is not possible anymore. Residence permits will depend on immigrants’ skills. The law also introduces a ‘golden visa’ for people who want to invest money in Hungary. These people can live in the country. Some parties don’t agree with the law. Difficult words: prioritize (to make something more important than something else), reunion (when two or more people come together again), residence permit (a document which says that a foreigner can live in a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Valentina Cafolla swiftly reclaimed her apnea ice diving world record, diving 140 meters deep without oxygen or assistance within just 36 hours. Initially setting the record in 2017, Cafolla’s achievement was surpassed by Yasuko Ozeki, only to be regained by Cafolla at Lago di Anterselva in the Italian Alps, despite challenging conditions. Her resilience and skill were evident as she faced heavy snowfall and icy waters. Additionally, Cafolla set a new world record with a double fin dive the following day, showcasing her remarkable talent and determination. Her story serves as an inspiration, highlighting the importance of perseverance and dedication in achieving one’s goals in the face of adversity. Difficult words: apnea (freediving), resilience (toughness), perseverance (the continued effort despite difficulties or failure). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
